title: Lesson Plan — Patterns in Mathematics (Class 6 CBSE)
subject: Mathematics
objectives: Explain that mathematics is, at its heart, the search for patterns.
Recognise the common number sequences: counting, even, odd, square, triangular, cube, powers of 2, Fibonacci.
Find the next term of a sequence by spotting the rule.
Use dot diagrams to visualise square and triangular numbers.
Apply the rules 1 + 3 + 5 + … + (2n − 1) = n^2 and triangular(n) = n(n + 1)/2.
Verify that two consecutive triangular numbers add to a square number.
materials: Square grid handouts (one per pair) for plotting dots
Coloured chalk or markers for drawing L-shapes inside grids
Worksheet — Patterns in Mathematics (one per student)
Cards labelled with sequences for a 'rule-spotting' card sort

activities.description: Hook with the famous Gauss problem: 'Find 1 + 2 + 3 + … + 100 in 30 seconds.' Let students try by hand. Reveal that triangular(100) = 100 × 101 / 2 = 5050 — and promise to derive the rule together.
teacher_actions: Pose the 1 to 100 sum and time 30 seconds.
Take three guesses; reveal the answer.
Promise the formula in the Explain phase.

activities.description: Pair card sort. Distribute cards labelled with sequences (1,2,3,…; 2,4,6,…; 1,4,9,…; 1,3,6,…; 1,1,2,3,5,…; 2,4,8,16,…). Pairs identify the rule for each.
teacher_actions: Pick two pairs to share their rules.
student_actions: Sort and identify the rule for each card.

activities.description: Direct instruction in three blocks: (i) common sequences with examples — counting, even, odd, square, triangular, cube, Fibonacci, powers of 2; (ii) drawing dot diagrams for square and triangular numbers; (iii) the two key formulas — sum of first n odd = n^2 and triangular(n) = n(n+1)/2 — with the L-shape and rectangle picture proofs.
teacher_actions: Build the sequence vocabulary on the board with one example each.
Draw a 4×4 grid of dots and trace L-shaped strips of 1, 3, 5, 7 dots — derive 1+3+5+7 = 16 = 4^2 visually.
Use a triangle of 4 rows to show triangular(4) = 10; tilt two copies to make a 4 × 5 rectangle.
student_actions: Predict the formula before the teacher writes it.
Add the two key formulas to a 'rules box'.

activities.description: Application station. Students do five worksheet problems: (1) find the next term of a sequence; (2) compute the 6th square number; (3) compute the 7th triangular number; (4) find sum of first 10 odd numbers using the formula; (5) verify triangular(5) + triangular(6) is a square.
teacher_actions: Circulate; offer the smallest hint that unblocks a stuck student.
Collect common slips for the Evaluate phase.
Pair fast finishers with peers who need support.
student_actions: Solve individually; compare with a partner.
Self-check against a posted answer key.
Verify each answer using a different method (dots, formula).

activities.description: Exit-ticket quiz: 5 questions drawn from the chapter bank. Students complete in 4 minutes. Project answers; brief discussion of the most-missed item.
teacher_actions: Distribute exit-ticket; remind students it is individual.

activities.description: Set homework: rest of the worksheet, plus one CREATE prompt — 'Make up a number sequence with a clear rule. List the first 5 terms and write the rule. Bonus: draw a shape that matches your sequence.' Preview the next chapter (Lines and Angles).
teacher_actions: Bridge to next chapter with a quick 'how many angles do you see?' prompt.

homework: Complete the remaining problems on the Worksheet — Patterns in Mathematics handout.
Make up a number sequence with a clear rule; list the first 5 terms and state the rule.
Optional: find a real-world pattern (flower petals, brick layout, stair steps) and explain its rule in 2–3 sentences.
assessment_ideas: Use the 5-item exit ticket as a quick formative check.
Set a 10-question quiz drawn from the chapter bank for the next class as summative.
Mark the LONG_ANSWER on the L-shape proof of 1+3+5+…=n^2 using the auto-grade rubric.
Run a 5-minute peer-grading round on the CREATE homework using a two-criterion rubric (clear rule? 5 correct terms?).
references: NCERT Class 6 Mathematics — Ganita Prakash, Chapter 1: Patterns in Mathematics.
